Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Man books Rs 1.55 lakh Delhi-New York round trip, airline changes flight itinerary without his consent and travel website rejects refund despite zero-cancellation policy; consumer commission orders Rs

A consumer commission in Visakhapatnam has directed a travel booking website and an airline to pay Rs 1.95 lakh to a passenger after finding them guilty of changing his international flight itinerary without obtaining his consent, ultimately leaving him unable to undertake the planned trip. The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the two companies to refund Rs 1.55 lakh to the passenger, pay Rs 30,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The complaint concerned a round-trip booking made by the passenger and his friend through the travel website. As per the original itinerary, they were scheduled to leave Delhi for New York on September 4, 2024, travel onwards to Miami and then Quito, before returning to Miami and New York. Their return journey to Delhi was scheduled for September 11, 2024.However, the passenger alleged that the flight timings were subsequently altered without his approval. He contacted the booking platform and told it that the revised schedule would not serve the purpose of his trip. He then sought cancellation of the tickets and a full refund, arguing that he had neither requested nor agreed to the changes. According to the complaint, the website continued sending him messages suggesting that the itinerary changes had been initiated at his request, despite the alterations being made by the airlines.His refund request was eventually rejected, although he had opted for a zero-cancellation policy.Defending itself, the travel website told the commission that the airline had made schedule changes after the tickets were confirmed. These changes were beyond its control and included the cancellation of the Miami-Quito flight. The website's counsel claimed that the passenger subsequently contacted the platform to explore alternative arrangements and that a revised itinerary was prepared at his request. When he later sought a refund, the airline refused it under its applicable policy.The counsel further argued that the zero-cancellation policy purchased by the passenger did not cover situations in which an airline rescheduled a flight from its originally scheduled time. The airline, meanwhile, argued that the changes had been communicated well before the scheduled journey and had not materially affected the passenger's travel plans. It alleged that the booking website had independently cancelled the original reservation and issued an entirely new itinerary.The airline also told the commission that it did not directly handle cancellations or refunds for bookings made through third-party agents. It said it had transferred Rs 14,545 to the travel website and that the responsibility for passing on the amount to the passenger rested with the platform. It further argued that the passenger and his friend had failed to check in for the first flight and were consequently marked as no-shows. According to the airline, standard international airline practice requires all subsequent sectors of an itinerary to be cancelled if a passenger does not board the first flight.The commission, however, found fault with the manner in which the original booking had been altered. It noted that the travel website had not responded to the passenger's specific allegation that his consent had never been obtained before changing the itinerary. The commission observed that the platform's silence on this issue indicated its acceptance of the allegation.The commission also took note of the website's admission that a new itinerary had been implemented despite the absence of the passenger's consent.It observed that the companies had unilaterally altered the travel plan without securing the passenger's approval. An intermediary acting prudently should not have initiated an alternative itinerary without obtaining written consent from the consumer, it said. Holding both the travel website and the airline liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, the commission directed them to refund Rs 1.55 lakh to the passenger, pay Rs 30,000 in compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs.
Article Summary: Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the two companies to refund Rs 1.55 lakh to the passenger, pay Rs 30,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The complaint concerned a round-trip booking made by the passenger and his friend through the travel website.

GURGAON: A dinner outing with friends in Gurgaon ended in a consumer dispute after a woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the restaurant to pay her Rs 31,000, including compensation for mental harassment and litigation expenses. It has also ordered a refund of the Rs 401 service charge.The dispute dates back to May 16, 2026, when the woman visited the restaurant with her friends for dinner. She alleged that the bill included a service charge of Rs 401, equivalent to 10% of the amount. She objected to the additional charge and asked the restaurant to remove it. However, the establishment allegedly refused, leaving her with no option but to pay the entire bill of Rs 4,811, including the disputed fee.The woman later approached the consumer commission, arguing that the restaurant had violated the Central Consumer Protection Authority's (CCPA) guidelines on service charges. The restaurant did not appear before the commission despite being given an opportunity to respond. The proceedings were therefore conducted ex parte.In its order, the commission referred to the CCPA's guidelines issued on July 4, 2022, which prohibit hotels and restaurants from automatically adding a service charge to bills.The guidelines state that establishments cannot collect such charges by default or under another name. They also make clear that payment of a service charge must remain voluntary, with consumers free to decide whether they want to pay it.The commission said the restaurant had disregarded these provisions by refusing to remove the charge despite the customer's objection. It held the establishment guilty of deficiency in service and adopting an unfair trade practice, observing that its actions amounted to a blatant violation of the CCPA guidelines. Apart from ordering the restaurant to return the Rs 401 collected as service charge, the commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss. It also directed the restaurant to pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses, taking the total amount payable to Rs 31,401, including the refund.
Article Summary: A woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has ordered the establishment to pay her Rs 31,000. The commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss.

Article Title: London homeowner ordered to pay £10,000 in damages after removing new neighbours' entrance on their moving-in day, with court ruling they had the right to drive across his land and install gates
Article Text:

Judge rejects neighbour's argument over couple's right of access

Why did the judge reject the neighbour's demands over gate placement

Judge condemns neighbour's conduct and orders £10,000 compensation

Disclaimer:

This article is based on a publicly available judgment by the Mayor’s and City of London Court. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the

property dispute

, the parties involved, or the court proceedings mentioned in the article.

A London homeowner was found to have destroyed a neighbour’s roller shutter as new owners moved in. The dispute concerned access rights and gates between two homes in Disbrowe Road. The defendant, Adrian Robert Udal, removed the barrier on 25 August 2023 and later installed metal gates. According to a judgment by the Mayor’s and City of London Court, the removal was wrongful destruction and interfered with the neighbours’ property rights.Judge HHJ Parfitt found the owners had rights to use the passageway on foot and by vehicle, and to install gates where reasonably required. Udal was ordered to pay the couple £10,000 in total compensation, including £2,500 for the removed structure and £7,500 in general damages.Nicholas George Kenly Partick-Hiley and Lise Marie Partick-Hiley completed the purchase of 1.5 Disbrowe Road on 25 August 2023. When they arrived to take possession, they found Udal and another person removing the roller shutter and door that separated their property from the street. The court heard that the claimants had previously been in discussions with Udal in an effort to address potential issues and establish a good neighbourly relationship.Udal owned and occupied 1 Disbrowe Road, which stood in front of the claimants’ home. Their property could only be reached through a driveway and passageway forming part of Udal’s freehold land.The dispute involved the meaning of rights recorded in a 1972 conveyance and a 1973 grant. Udal argued that the neighbours’ right to use the passageway did not include vehicles and applied only to part of the route. Judge Parfitt rejected that interpretation.The court found that the 1973 grant gave the owners of 1.5 Disbrowe Road the right to pass and repass over the disputed passage, on foot or with or without vehicles. The judge said the wording covered the whole route and reflected the practical need to reach the property. The court therefore confirmed that the neighbours were entitled to use the passageway for vehicle access as well as on foot.The claimants also argued that they had the right to put gates across the disputed passageway at a position they reasonably required. Udal maintained that any gates had to be fitted between two front pillars. The judge disagreed, finding that the relevant wording of the 1972 conveyance allowed the owners of 1.5 Disbrowe Road to install gates wherever they reasonably required them on the passageway.The court considered the location sought by the claimants reasonable. It also found that Udal’s own metal gates, installed on the front pillars in September 2023 without the claimants’ agreement, interfered with their rights. The gates were unnecessary and obstructed the claimants’ ability to exercise their rights.Judge Parfitt described Udal’s removal of the roller shutter and associated fittings as an inappropriate and wrongful act of wanton destruction. The court found that the removal amounted to trespass to property and that his wider conduct constituted nuisance and wrongful interference with the neighbours’ rights. It awarded the claimants £2,500 to reflect the cost of replacing the removed structure.The judge also awarded £7,500 in general damages, taking account of the upset and discomfort caused by Udal’s actions and their effect on the claimants’ enjoyment of their home. The court said declarations and injunctions were needed to protect the neighbours’ rights and limit the risk of similar interference happening again.
Article Summary: Neighbour removes couple's entrance on their first day in new home. Judge rejects neighbour's argument over couple's right of access. Judge condemns neighbour's conduct and orders £10,000 compensation. The dispute concerned access rights and gates between two homes in Disbrowe Road.

Article Title: In 2025, Alabama Power offered a landowner $80,000 for an easement across his property; in 2026, he won a ruling against its 300-foot exclusion request as the fight over his 416 acres continues
Article Text:

A dispute over a sprawling Alabama property has taken another turn after a judge rejected a utility company’s attempt to keep the landowner away from construction crews working on his land. Alabama Power has now taken the matter to the state’s highest court, prolonging a legal battle over a major electricity transmission project. According to reports by WVTM 13, 1819 News and Birmingham Free Press, the dispute centres on 416 acres owned by Fenn Church near Calera in Shelby County, where the company is seeking to build part of a 74-mile transmission line. The latest development came on November 10, when Shelby County Circuit Judge Jonathan Spann denied Alabama Power’s request for a temporary restraining order that would have required Church and visitors to remain at least 300 feet away from crews clearing trees on the property. The judge dismissed the case without prejudice, meaning the utility is not permanently barred from pursuing similar legal relief.Alabama Power subsequently filed a notice of appeal with the Alabama Supreme Court, seeking to challenge the decision. The company is also seeking transcripts and other court records as part of the appeal. The immediate disagreement centres on the company’s efforts to clear a construction corridor through Church’s land.Alabama Power maintains that the exclusion zone is necessary to protect the property owner, visitors and workers operating heavy machinery. Church, however, has opposed further clearing while his separate legal challenge to the easement remains unresolved.The disagreement has already resulted in several confrontations between Church and construction crews. According to earlier reporting by WVTM 13, workers had cleared hundreds of yards of the proposed corridor, including sections containing mature oak trees. Church has objected to the removal of vegetation and has repeatedly attempted to prevent crews from continuing their work.The wider dispute dates back to January 2025, when Alabama Power reportedly offered Church $80,000 for a permanent easement across his property. Subsequent offers increased to $132,000 in September 2025 and $194,000 in May this year, according to court-related details reported by Birmingham Free Press.After negotiations failed, Alabama Power pursued eminent domain proceedings to secure the rights required for the project. On August 4, 2026, a probate court awarded Church $425,435 for the easement and access road rights. The compensation covers the utility’s right to use the designated portion of the property, not ownership of the entire land. Church challenged the award, and the separate condemnation case remains pending.The legal situation shifted again in September, when Judge Spann granted Church a preliminary injunction preventing Alabama Power from entering his property while the condemnation dispute continued. However, the Alabama Supreme Court stayed that injunction on October 21, allowing the utility to resume work. Crews returned to the property the following day.Alabama Power maintains that it has secured the necessary easement rights and that delays could jeopardise the project’s planned completion in May 2027. The Autaugaville-East Pelham 230-kilovolt transmission line is a 74-mile infrastructure project connecting the Montgomery and Birmingham areas. The company says it is needed to strengthen electricity supply for approximately three million customers across Alabama.Church has also raised the possibility of an alternative route through adjoining properties, arguing that the existing alignment would significantly affect his land and privacy. Alabama Power, however, has said that proposed alternatives were evaluated and considered unfeasible, citing additional costs, construction complications and potential delays. With the latest appeal, the dispute now has another legal chapter ahead. While Alabama Power continues to defend its right to carry out the project, Church’s challenge to the condemnation and the company’s use of his property remains unresolved.
Article Summary: Fenn Church owns 416 acres near Calera in Shelby County, Alabama. Alabama Power is seeking to build part of a 74-mile transmission line on his land. Church has objected to the removal of vegetation and has repeatedly attempted to prevent crews from continuing their work. On November 10, a judge denied Alabama Power's request for a temporary restraining order.

Article Title: Nvidia spy scandal: What Jensen Huang told top executives about his relationship with Alice Huang
Article Text:
Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled some of the chipmaker's senior executives about his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. He portrayed their interactions as routine business dealings, despite having an affair with her, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.Among the executives Huang communicated with were general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld. In two separate messages sent in October, Huang told them that his interactions with Alice Huang were part of standard business dealings with customers. He also described his engagement with her company, Megaspeed International, as routine in other communications, people told Reuters.Also Read| Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit may cost him around Rs 900 crore: How much wealth does he have left? Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on the condition that the messages would not be quoted verbatim. The news agency is the first to report on the correspondence.The two people said Huang had addressed questions about his relationship with Alice Huang on two occasions, during the autumn of 2025 and again in October 2026, after press queries brought the matter to the attention of some Nvidia leaders. On both occasions, he described their interactions as appropriate. Reuters reviewed only the October messages and not the exchanges from 2025.Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer, was under investigation by the US over suspicions that she may have been spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share the same surname but are not related.Huang's interactions with Alice Huang had come under scrutiny following a New York Times article published in October last year, which highlighted their public meetings. According to the two people, Huang subsequently discussed the possibility of taking legal action against the newspaper.The article had also prompted him to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about his interactions with Alice Huang. However, he did not describe the relationship as an affair, the people said.Neither Huang nor Nvidia eventually sued the newspaper. A spokesperson for the New York Times said it had received no legal demand.It remains unclear when the relationship became intimate.
